newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges Sinn Finn to accept Blair's offer.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges Sinn Finn to accept Blair's offer.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Friday praised British Prime Minister Tony Blair's offer of talks with Sinn Fein and pressed the IRA's political wing to accept Blair's offer.

On a trip to Northern Ireland, his first outside London since his Labour Party won a general election on May 1, Blair offered talks between British officials and Sinn Fein without demanding a formal IRA ceasefire first.

"I welcome Prime Minister Blair's statement today in Northern Ireland as a balanced and contructive step toward restoring momentum to the peace process. His words offer hope and reassurance to the people of both of Northern Ireland's traditions," Clinton said in a written statement.
The president noted that Blair's government, like its predecessor, would invite Sinn Fein to the negotiating table only on the basis of an unequivocal ceasefire.

Blair "has taken the initiative in offering to meet with Sinn Fein, at the official level, to assess whether inclusive talks are possible on that basis. I urge Sinn Fein to take up this offer," Clinton said.

"Now is the time to open a new chapter in the history of this tragic conflict and achieve through dialogue and negotiation the lasting settlement the people of Northern Ireland want and deserve," Clinton said.
